_comment: Paired measurements used to calibrate and validate the CPU estimate.
cycles: measured ON HARDWARE with plaits/cpu_probe.h (DWT cycle counter,
inside the real audio interrupt), read off the AUX tone of a --stock-bench
firmware while stepping the model knob through all sixteen engines.
counts: measured under QEMU's mps2-an386 (Cortex-M4) with the TCG plugin in
cycles_plugin.c, built by the same arm-4.8.3 toolchain as the firmware.
Conditions: HARMONICS/TIMBRE/MORPH/FREQUENCY at centre, nothing patched.
The percussion engines therefore run in sustain mode (trigger unpatched),
which is their full-cost path -- their render is unconditional, with no
early-out when idle.
These are REAL engines on purpose. An earlier attempt calibrated on
synthetic workloads that each did one thing exclusively; those spread
cycles-per-instruction 1.01 to 15.54 and predicted nothing, because real
engines are mixtures and mixtures average. Measured on real engines the
spread is 1.75x.
inharmonic-string is a genuine outlier at 11.9 cycles/instruction. Pitch,
memory traffic, denormals, state build-up and divide count were each tested
and each refuted. It is retained rather than dropped: it is the evidence
that a static estimate can be badly wrong, and the basis for the failure
rate the estimate reports.

_provenance.hardware: Plaits, STM32F373 @ 72 MHz, 48 kHz, block size 12
_provenance.two_engines_merged: virtual-analog and wave-terrain read the same plateau (990); their individual costs are within measurement resolution of each other
